note: PASS with caveats. (1) LANGUAGE: the paper's Methods state the study used 'the ERQ-C, which was translated by Wang et al. [7]', administered online via Sojump to native-Chinese-speaking students in Jiangsu. Files checked for Chinese wording: the article XML (all six tables and body text; items referred to only as Q1-Q10) and the single supplement S1 File (one data sheet with headers ID, Gender, ERQr1..ERQr10 plus two empty sheets, no item text in any language). Neither holds any item wording, so the Step-4 fallback applies: canonical English ERQ in the base fields, language=Chinese, _translated columns empty, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=official_instrument_english. The ERQ-C Chinese wording was not hunted off-source. (2) MAPPING: the item code IS the S1 column name (data/zhao_2024_erq.py melts ERQ* columns by name). The codes carry no text; the tie from code number k to canonical ERQ item k is the instrument's printed numbering, the same basis as moe2025_erq/morales_2021_erq. The r/s letter in each code matches Gross & John's scoring key exactly (reappraisal 1,3,5,7,8,10; suppression 2,4,6,9). Verified with verify_zhao_2024_erq.R: the canonical 6/4 split ranks 1st of 210 by within-minus-between inter-item r (0.430 vs runner-up 0.164), and refitting the paper's two-factor CFA (MLM) on the live data reproduces all 18 standardised loadings in Table 3 (10-item and 8-item models) to within 0.0005, and Table 4's alphas (0.840/0.745) exactly, tying each live code to the paper's own Q-number. The paper drops Q1 and Q3 to form the ERQ-8, which is the ERQ-8 literature's removal of canonical items 1 and 3, consistent with Q-numbers being canonical numbers. PARTIAL: nothing establishes which canonical wording each Q-number carries within a subscale beyond the instrument's numbering. Minor non-reproductions, not mapping-relevant: lavaan's scaled chi-square 130.34/34 and 42.52/19 vs Mplus 132.219/34 and 43.010/19; factor correlation 0.105 vs published 0.084. (3) OPTION TEXT: the ERQ form labels only 1 'strongly disagree', 4 'neutral', 7 'strongly agree'; points 2,3,5,6 left blank, not padded. The paper describes the anchors as '1' complete disagreement and '7' total agreement; the ERQ-C's own Chinese anchors are not recoverable from the deposit. (4) RIGHTS: applied, not re-derived -- ben-domingue's 2026-09-08 ruling (irw#2121) that Gross & John's English ERQ from Gross's lab page ships; the page's only term is 'The measures provided here may be used for academic research purposes with appropriate citation.' (as quoted in batch_108/moe2025_erq). instrument_rights_register.csv still has no ERQ row. (5) The instructions paragraph is Gross's English form text; the ERQ-C instructions actually shown are unknown.
public_note: The ERQ was administered in Chinese (the ERQ-C translation of Wang et al.), but neither the PLOS ONE paper nor its data supplement contains any item wording in either language -- the data columns are bare codes ERQr1-ERQr10 -- so the item text shown here is Gross and John's (2003) canonical English ERQ rather than the sentences participants read. Item codes follow the instrument's printed item numbers; the reappraisal (r) / suppression (s) split is confirmed by the data and every code reproduces the paper's published factor loadings, but nothing in the data distinguishes items within a subscale by wording. Scale points 2, 3, 5 and 6 carry no option text because the ERQ form labels only 1, 4 and 7.
